stem: A nurse is comparing hospitals for transfer of a client who may need advanced stroke care. What does Joint Commission Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) certification indicate?

options.A: The hospital has met Joint Commission advanced stroke-certification requirements that include core disease-specific standards plus additional stroke-specific requirements, evidence-based clinical practice processes, and performance measurement.
options.B: Any hospital can use the CSC designation regardless of stroke resources, patient volume, standardized care processes, or certification review.
options.C: CSC is a basic rehabilitation-only designation and does not indicate an advanced acute-stroke program.
options.D: CSC certification means performance measurement is unnecessary once the initial certification review is passed.

rationale: A is correct. The Joint Commission classifies Comprehensive Stroke Center certification as an advanced stroke certification developed with the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association. Advanced certification requires the core Disease-Specific Care requirements plus additional clinically specific requirements, use of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines, and ongoing performance measurement. B, C, and D contradict the certification framework. Specific transfer decisions still depend on the patient's clinical needs and the receiving hospital's current capabilities and availability; certification does not replace real-time transfer assessment.
educational_objective: Interpret Comprehensive Stroke Center certification as evidence that a hospital has met an advanced, externally reviewed stroke-care framework with stroke-specific standards, evidence-based care processes, and performance measurement, while continuing to verify real-time transfer capability for the individual client.
source_organization: The Joint Commission in collaboration with the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association
source_document_title: Stroke Certification; What Is Certification?; 2026 Stroke Certification Standards
source_version_date: 2026 Stroke Certification Standards released October 20, 2025; current Joint Commission pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Stroke Certification — Comprehensive Stroke Center is one of the Joint Commission's advanced stroke certifications; advanced programs meet core Disease-Specific Care requirements plus additional clinically specific requirements. Certification Standards — certification framework includes standards, clinical practice guidelines, and performance measurement. What Is Certification? — eligible programs use standardized evidence-based care methods and performance measurement to improve over time. 2026 Stroke Certification Standards contains the requirements to achieve and maintain CSC certification.
source_claim_supported: Joint Commission CSC certification is an advanced stroke-care certification requiring compliance with disease-specific and stroke-specific standards, evidence-based care processes, and performance measurement; it is not an unrestricted label available to any hospital.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: use appropriate organizational and referral resources, coordinate transfers, and participate in quality-improvement systems.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interpreting stroke-center certification for referral and transfer
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw CSC item to avoid asserting unverified operational details such as a universal 24/7 thrombectomy wording from a public summary page. The final item uses the current 2026 Joint Commission certification framework and tests what advanced CSC certification reliably signifies while preserving the need for real-time transfer-capability verification.

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current Joint Commission stroke-certification pages and the 2026 Stroke Certification Standards publication.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reflects the documented advanced-certification framework. B denies eligibility/review requirements. C incorrectly makes CSC a basic rehabilitation designation. D contradicts ongoing performance-measure requirements.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; advanced certification with standards, evidence-based processes, and measurement.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; certification has defined eligibility and review requirements.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; CSC is an advanced acute-stroke certification.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; performance measurement is an ongoing certification component.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A states what can be verified from the current official certification framework without assuming a specific capability is available at a particular moment.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe the meaning and governance of CSC certification.
